title: Shadow-run interop harness for hybrid streaming + tool-call migrations
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: Recent API version work introduced behavioral flags for streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. We must ensure deprecations and new behavior flags do not cause regressions across client versions, especially when streaming and tool-calls interact (e.g., partial streamed tool invocations, mid-stream function call triggers).

Goal: Build a repeatable shadow-run harness that: (1) replays live traffic against new behavior-flagged codepaths without impacting production responses, (2) exercises hybrid scenarios (streaming + tool-calls + structured output schemas), (3) produces deterministic regressions reports and regression-level metrics that map to customer-facing features.

Scope: - Implement a shadow routing layer in the API gateway to fork 5% of production requests to the harness. - Support three modes: full-snapshot replay, prefix re-simulation, and synthetic macro-scenarios (long streaming sessions and multi-call tool sequences). - Add deterministic diffing for token-level outputs, tool-call invocation sequences, and structured JSON schema mismatches. - Generate per-request regression severity (none | minor | major | blocking) with trace links to logs, PRs, and evaluation prompts.

Out of scope: - End-to-end customer-facing migration guide (PM will own separate doc). - On-prem runtime changes beyond agent-compatible telemetry hooks.
tasks: Design: define shadow schema and diff heuristics (token alignment, tool-call identity, semantic similarity thresholds)
Gateway: add non-blocking fork path that sends copies to harness with metadata headers (x-redwood-shadow: ENG-27109)
Harness: implement runner that replays requests into staging runtime instances and captures outputs and tool-call traces
Diff: implement token-level and semantic diff processor + structured output schema validator
Dashboard: add regression dashboard with filters (model, client-version, route, flag-state)
Test plan: run 48-hour mirrored run, measure regression rates, and produce report
acceptance_criteria: Shadow fork does not add >1ms to median API latency for production requests
Captured traffic covers at least 80% of streaming+toolcall routes in the first 24h for the 5% sample
Diff engine labels regressions with precision >= 90% on a curated evaluation set
Regression dashboard surfaces trace links and suggested next-step labels (bug, behavior-change, benign)
Runbook for enabling/disabling shadow for a specific route without a deploy exists
test_plan: Phase 1: Local run with synthetic streaming+toolcall sequences and unit tests for diff logic. Phase 2: Canary mirrored traffic using internal staging model for 24h. Phase 3: 5% production shadow run with full capture and nightly regression report. Metrics to monitor: forked_request_rate, harness_processing_time, diff_rate, false_positive_rate_on_eval_set, resource_cost_delta. Collect example failures into a triage mailbox.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge harness feature branch behind feature flag. 2) Enable gateway fork for internal-only traffic. 3) Enable canary fork for a small internal customer to exercise regression surface. 4) After 48h of stability, open production 5% sample. 5) If regressions > threshold (major >0.5% or blocking >0.05%), pause fork and create follow-up ENG tickets.
rollback_plan: Gateway can toggle fork header to 0%; harness is non-blocking so disabling fork immediately stops load. Post-mortem steps and automatic alerts to oncall and PM.
notes: Design trade-offs: we prefer conservative semantic diffs (reduce noise) and will iterate thresholds with PM and infra. Need coordination with SRE for cost budgeting; the harness increases staging instance usage during peak. Consider adding sampling by route weight to prioritize high-risk endpoints (streaming+tool-calls).
